dialect.detail: IBM DB2 COBOL with QUERYNO clauses, FETCH FIRST ROW ONLY, CASE expressions in SQL, and ¬= operator (EBCDIC not-equal sign) — all characteristic of IBM mainframe DB2 embedded SQL
evidence: CASE WHEN ... THEN ... END in SQL

purpose.domain_detail: Retail grocery/supermarket system dealing with UPC items, food stamps, coupons, store ROG (Ring of Goods) codes, and corporate item codes
purpose.summary: A test/snippet program containing several embedded DB2 SQL statements used in a retail grocery context. It includes a cursor declaration for food stamp data, a SELECT with complex CASE-based ROG filtering, a DELETE from a COUPON table, a COALESCE COUNT query, and OPEN/CLOSE cursor operations. The program appears to be a collection of SQL test cases rather than a complete production program.

notable_features: CASE expressions inside SQL WHERE clause
No DATA DIVISION or ENVIRONMENT DIVISION
No PIC clauses or host variable declarations in visible code
verdict.notes: The program has no DATA DIVISION, ENVIRONMENT DIVISION, or host variable declarations — it is clearly a snippet or test file containing only SQL statement examples. The ¬= operator is the EBCDIC not-equal sign, confirming IBM mainframe origin. The filename 'testdb2.cbl' and the pattern of multiple disconnected paragraphs each containing one SQL statement strongly suggest this is a test/reference file for DB2 SQL syntax rather than a runnable production program.
